_comment: Register pointers whose cited LINE CONTENT differs from the revision that wrote them, each with a written `reason` saying which PR re-pins it or why nothing does. The screen FAILS on any drift not listed here and reports entries that no longer drift as STALE (non-failing, prune them). `regLines` are the register sentences the cite silences — the screen matches on cite, so one entry can cover several. Regenerate preserving reasons: node scripts/check-register-drift.mjs --update

entries.reason: Read-log, not a pointer: PP-055 lists the auto-backup line set (55, 147, 243, 256-257, 297) as ranges somebody read, and #2441 declined to re-pin it for exactly that reason — re-pinning would invent an intent the entry never stated. Listed here so the decision is on the record instead of silent drift.

Chronic, not accidental: the register's header bullets and entry sections quote this README sentence, and that sentence is the README's own re-pin of a pointer INTO the register - so any entry that adds register header text moves the line the pointer names, and this cite reads as drift by construction. PP-072 (#2558) minted it with the rule at :4651, PP-073 (#2567) moved it to :4774, PP-065 (#2507) to :4810, PP-074 (#2526, shipped as #2568) to :4940, PP-070 (#2534, since merged) to :5013, the #2566 addendum to :5079 (the fourteenth, and the first that mints no entry of its own), PP-075 (#2560, shipped as #2569) to :5172, PP-076 (#2561, shipped as #2581) re-pinned it to :5194, PP-078 (#2587) to :5312, and this merge of #2578 adds PP-077's header bullet, summary row and section above the rule too, so the sentence now reads :5425. The number is per-tree: #2569 measures its own lines because both edit the same header, so whichever merges last re-derives this entry. Prune it the day the README points at the rule by heading text instead of a line number.

History, not a live pointer: the register's PP-068 bullet reports the coordinate as it found it - `docs/README.md:90` is where the README's kept-rather-than-deleted paragraph sat when that bullet was written, and the sentence it names is the README's own re-pin of a pointer INTO the register, so any entry that adds register header text moves the line the pointer names and this cite reads as drift by construction. #3410 re-pinned it from `:71` to `:90` on 2026-11-05 because the branch's census entry grew the README above it 3 lines, and the merge of `main` moved it again; re-writing PP-068's sentence would falsify the measurement it reports. Prune it the day the README names the rule by heading text instead of a line number.
